# Identify file locations and load libraries

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(tidyverse)

input_file <- "../data/raw/03-all_metrics_sample-level.csv"
output_dir <- file.path("../data/cleaned", "v01")
dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# IMPORTANT: All alteration switches are OFF until supported by the decision log.
replace_nonpositive_p450_with_na <- FALSE
replace_nonpositive_sod_with_loq <- TRUE

# Do not set the value below without checking the actual assay LOD / LOQ,
# original units, and whether this substitution is justified.
sod_replacement_value <- 0.025

```

# 2. Read and preserve the original

```{r}
#| label: import
raw_data <- read_csv(input_file, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(sample_id = as.character(sample_id),
         site_number = as.character(site_number),
         reporting_area = as.character(reporting_area))

required_columns <- c("sample_id", "site_number", "reporting_area", "p450", "sod",
                      "shell", "condition_index", "weight_initial", "weight_final",
                      "weight_change", "length", "width", "height")
stopifnot(file.exists(input_file))
stopifnot(all(required_columns %in% names(raw_data)))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(raw_data$sample_id))

# Do not edit raw_data. This separate object receives any approved changes.
clean_data <- raw_data

glimpse(raw_data)
summary(raw_data)
```

# 3. Assemble a review queue (not a deletion list)

The next table identifies cases the older cleaning script would have changed. It is **not** a decision about whether the original observation is invalid. Use source bench notes, kit guidance, detection limits, and existing EDA flags to resolve each case.

```{r}
#| label: review-queue
review_queue <- raw_data %>%
  select(sample_id, site_number, p450, sod) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(p450, sod), names_to = "metric", values_to = "original_value") %>%
  filter(is.na(original_value) | original_value <= 0) %>%
  mutate(issue_or_flag = case_when(
    is.na(original_value) ~ "Original value is missing",
    original_value == 0 ~ "Zero value: verify assay definition",
    original_value < 0 ~ "Negative value: verify assay definition")) %>%
  arrange(metric, site_number, sample_id)

review_queue
write_csv(review_queue, file.path(output_dir, "01_nonpositive_and_missing_REVIEW.csv"))
```


# 4. Document the decision *before* changing the data

Use the separate cleaning-decision log template or create a new blank log. The review queue above is evidence for the log; it is not a substitute for explaining the rule and verifying the original records. The template is not overwritten when the report is rendered again.

```{r}
#| label: decision-log
log_path <- file.path(output_dir, "02_cleaning_decision_log.csv")
if (!file.exists(log_path)) {
  decision_log <- tibble(sample_id = character(),
                         site_number = character(),
                         metric = character(),
                         original_value = double(),
                         issue_or_flag = character(),
                         source_evidence = character(),
                         decision = character(),
                         reason = character(),
                         approved_by = character(),
                         new_value = double(),
                         decision_date = character(),
                         notes = character())
  write_csv(decision_log, log_path)
}
```

## 4.1 Decision questions

1. Is the value observed, below a detection or quantification threshold, an error, or missing by design?
2. Is the reported limit in the **same units** as the finalized normalized biomarker activity?
3. Will the rule apply to every affected observation, or only specified sample IDs supported by lab records?
4. How will missing values enter site means and later models?
5. If an outlier is retained, how will the decision be explained? Retention can be the correct choice.

# 5. Apply the approved P450 rule (optional)

The historical script converted nonpositive P450 to missing. This may be appropriate for an invalid assay result, but **zero by itself does not prove invalidity**. If confirmed and approved, change the switch in Section 1; the code will document which values were altered.

```{r}
#| label: p450-decision
if (replace_nonpositive_p450_with_na) {
  clean_data <- clean_data %>%
    mutate(p450 = if_else(!is.na(p450) & p450 <= 0, NA_real_, p450))
}
```

# 6. Apply the approved SOD rule (optional)

Do not run a replacement until the replacement value and its analytical basis are verified. A threshold expressed in concentration units may not be directly applicable to the *protein-normalized activity result* without knowing the assay calculation and definitions. The following guard prevents an unverified missing replacement value.

```{r}
#| label: sod-decision
if (replace_nonpositive_sod_with_loq) {
  stopifnot(is.finite(sod_replacement_value))
  stopifnot(sod_replacement_value > 0)

  clean_data <- clean_data %>%
    mutate(sod = if_else(!is.na(sod) & sod <= 0,
                         sod_replacement_value, sod))
}
```

# 7. Example: correct an individual documented transcription error

If a bench record proves that **one sample × metric** value was transcribed incorrectly, make the change explicitly below. Replace the placeholders with the *verified* values; keep this section commented out until then. Avoid automatically replacing every outlier.

```{r}
#| label: one-off-example
# Example ONLY (do not run without source evidence and a log entry):
# clean_data <- clean_data %>%
#   mutate(shell = if_else(sample_id == "VERIFIED_SAMPLE_ID",
#                          VERIFIED_SHELL_VALUE, shell))
```

# 8. Check the outcome of cleaning

Compare **counts and original-versus-resulting values**, not merely the appearance of a plot. An altered, excluded, or retained observation must be traceable to a documented rule.

```{r}
#| label: audit-changes
changes <- raw_data %>%
  select(sample_id, site_number, p450, sod) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(p450, sod), names_to = "metric", values_to = "original_value") %>%
  left_join(
    clean_data %>%
      select(sample_id, p450, sod) %>%
      pivot_longer(cols = c(p450, sod), names_to = "metric", values_to = "new_value"),
    by = c("sample_id", "metric")) %>%
  mutate(changed = (is.na(original_value) != is.na(new_value)) |
           (!is.na(original_value) & !is.na(new_value) & original_value != new_value)) %>%
  filter(changed) %>%
  arrange(metric, sample_id)

changes
nrow(changes)

comparison <- bind_rows(
  raw_data %>%
    summarise(version = "original", n_samples = n(), n_sites = n_distinct(site_number),
              n_p450_missing = sum(is.na(p450)), n_sod_missing = sum(is.na(sod)),
              n_p450_nonpositive = sum(p450 <= 0, na.rm = TRUE),
              n_sod_nonpositive = sum(sod <= 0, na.rm = TRUE)),
  clean_data %>%
    summarise(version = "after_approved_rules", n_samples = n(), n_sites = n_distinct(site_number),
              n_p450_missing = sum(is.na(p450)), n_sod_missing = sum(is.na(sod)),
              n_p450_nonpositive = sum(p450 <= 0, na.rm = TRUE),
              n_sod_nonpositive = sum(sod <= 0, na.rm = TRUE))
)
comparison
```

## 8.1 Keep sample and site identifiers intact

```{r}
#| label: final-identity-check
stopifnot(nrow(clean_data) == nrow(raw_data))
stopifnot(identical(clean_data$sample_id, raw_data$sample_id))
stopifnot(identical(clean_data$site_number, raw_data$site_number))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(clean_data$sample_id))
```

# 9. Create a descriptive site-level data table

The old cleaning file averaged measurements at each site. Preserve this as a **separate derived table**, not a replacement for the sample-level file. Missing values are omitted *for each mean only*. When every value of a metric is missing at a site, the result should be `NA`, not `NaN`. The explicitly named fields make the operation transparent for beginning students.

```{r}
#| label: site-averages
site_means <- clean_data %>%
  group_by(site_number, site_name, reporting_area, latitude, longitude) %>%
  summarise(
    n_mussels = n(),
    n_p450 = sum(!is.na(p450)),
    n_sod = sum(!is.na(sod)),
    p450 = if_else(n_p450 > 0, mean(p450, na.rm = TRUE), NA_real_),
    sod = if_else(n_sod > 0, mean(sod, na.rm = TRUE), NA_real_),
    shell = mean(shell, na.rm = TRUE),
    condition_index = mean(condition_index, na.rm = TRUE),
    weight_initial = mean(weight_initial, na.rm = TRUE),
    weight_final = mean(weight_final, na.rm = TRUE),
    weight_change = mean(weight_change, na.rm = TRUE),
    length = mean(length, na.rm = TRUE),
    width = mean(width, na.rm = TRUE),
    height = mean(height, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

site_means
```

**Teaching note:** grouping on metadata fields assumes they are already reconciled by the separate source-file checklist. If a site splits into multiple rows because of inconsistent labels or coordinates, return to that checklist instead of treating the new rows as independent sites.

# 10. Export versioned files

This is the only place the cleaned dataset is exported. It writes a **new file**; it does not overwrite the input. Even if no rules are enabled, the result is a useful unchanged *baseline* for testing the teaching pipeline, but do not call it a cleaned analytical dataset until the decisions are completed.

```{r}
#| label: export
write_csv(clean_data, file.path(output_dir, "04-all_metrics_sample-level_CLEANED.csv"),
          na = "NA")
write_csv(site_means, file.path(output_dir, "05-all_metrics_site-level_DESCRIPTIVE.csv"),
          na = "NA")
write_csv(changes, file.path(output_dir, "03_implemented_changes.csv"), na = "NA")
write_csv(comparison, file.path(output_dir, "04_pre_post_rule_counts.csv"))

list.files(output_dir)
```

# 11. Return to the same EDA report

In `biomarker_combined_EDA_pre_post_WITH_FIGURES.qmd`, set:

```r
input_file <- "cleaning_output/v01/04-all_metrics_sample-level_CLEANED.csv"
run_label <- "post_cleaning"
```

Compare pre/post distributions, completeness, flags, site means, and figure exports. If no rule has yet been approved, pre/post figures should agree; that is expected. Changes in distribution, a smaller number of flags, or a higher Shapiro–Wilk p-value do **not** independently demonstrate that cleaning was correct. Record any further decisions, revise the cleaning version if necessary, and repeat the comparison before statistical analysis.
